title: Understanding Zero-One Loss
text: Zero-one loss is a simple way to measure the accuracy of predictions. It assigns a loss of $$1$$ for each incorrect prediction and $$0$$ for each correct one. Think about how many predictions are incorrect given the true labels and predicted probabilities.

title: Applying the Threshold
text: To determine the predicted labels, compare each predicted probability to the threshold T. If the probability is greater than T, the predicted label is 1; otherwise, it's $$0$$. Try applying this to each probability.

title: Calculate Predicted Labels
text: What are the predicted labels when you apply the threshold $$T=0.5$$ to the probabilities $$(0.1$$, $$0.6$$, $$0.9)$$?

title: Comparing True and Predicted Labels
text: Now that you have the predicted labels, compare them to the true labels (0, $$0$$, 1). Count how many times they differ to find the zero-one loss.

title: Calculate Zero-One Loss
text: How many of the predicted labels differ from the true labels?
